From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightpay.ai>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity buffer for end-of-month payroll

Hi Lukas,

We have an upcoming payroll run on May 30 that historically drives a short, sharp spike in inference requests (around run-time token peaks). Our SREs ran a simulation and estimate a ~3x increase in sustained token volume for ~6 hours during the window.

Can Redwood provision a short-term headroom buffer (temporary quota increase) and what would the surcharge/overage approach look like? Procurement also asked whether you offer invoice smoothing or a staged true-up vs immediate overrun billing — they'd prefer amortized impact across the next invoice if possible.

We may need the uplift by Tue 26th EOD to validate in staging. Who should I loop in for a contract amendment and a PO?

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform 
BrightPay

[Attached: none]

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightpay.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity buffer for end-of-month payroll

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the clear timeline. TL;DR: we can offer a provisional inflight cap bridge with a tiered surcharge and an optional amortized true-up that spreads the surcharge across the following invoice cycle.

Proposal (provisional):
- Temporary capacity uplift: +300% quota on your production route for a 48-hour window (configurable; specify exact start time).
- Tiered surcharge model applied to overrun tokens during the uplift window:
  * First 25M overrun tokens: +8% on your effective per-token rate
  * Next 75M overrun tokens: +5%
  * Beyond that: standard overrun rate (no extra uplift)
- Invoice smoothing option: Redwood can amortize the surcharge across the next invoice (one-period smoothing) or split across two invoices if procurement requires lower per-invoice impact.
- Credit guardrail: if the uplift is unused (we provision but traffic does not hit the uplifted headroom) you will not be charged the surcharge — charges are only on actual overrun tokens.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm exact uplift window start/end and whether you want 48h or 72h.
2) If procurement requires a PO, Marissa can produce a line-item cost estimate; Ben can run the provisional invoice and smoothing options.
3) We will prepare a short amendment (DocuSign) that records the temporary uplift and surcharge bands.

I cc'ed Marissa (account lead) and Ben (finance) for cost breakdown / DocuSign. If you want a faster turnaround, we can do a provisional approval and follow with formal amendment post-event.

Regards,
Lukas Meyer
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

- Procurement wants a simple line item they can put on a PO. Can you provide a per-hour estimated cost for the uplift window (best-effort based on your forecast) and a separate line for the maximum surcharge exposure?
- Would Redwood consider a 10% one-time credits offset if BrightPay signs the amendment for a recurring commit that upgrades our baseline after the payroll event? That would help internal approval.
- For the smoothing: procurement prefers split across two invoices (June and July) rather than one larger June hit. Is that acceptable?

Provisional estimate (48-hour uplift window, start 2027-05-26 18:00 PDT):
- Baseline blended rate: $0.0009 per token
- Estimated incremental tokens during window: 85,000,000 tokens
- Tiered surcharge calculation (applies only to actual overrun tokens during uplift):
  * First 25,000,000 tokens: +8% => surcharge cost: $1,800
  * Next 60,000,000 tokens: +5% => surcharge cost: $2,700
- Total surcharge estimate: $4,500
- If you elect two-invoice smoothing: we will amortize $2,250 to June invoice and $2,250 to July invoice.

Credit ask: we can offer a one-time account credit equal to 7% of the surcharge (instead of 10%) if BrightPay signs an amendment to move to a higher committed baseline within 30 days. The 7% credit is conditional on executed DocuSign within that window.
